summary: Final update, validated (valid; single effect: the statement of the recovery-value family fact). It narrows an over-broad premise in clause (a). That clause previously said startRecoveryForInstance fabricates a value ballot for its own empty state and the adoption loop therefore skips genuine replies, which is only true when the fabricated ballot sits above the peers' stored value ballots - the non-owner case, measured by the value-adoption receipt where replies at value ballot 0 were passed over against a fabricated ballot of 8. The clause now names the ballot rule itself (the recoverer's own id for the instance owner, id + N for any other recoverer, never advancing while IsLeader is false), the branch where genuine replies are skipped, and the owner branch where the fabricated ballot equals the peers' value ballot so their replies are still adopted - the equality case that clause (d) and the delivery-order receipts depend on - with the source lines for the ballot rule included and no other clause, condition, citation or execution touched. Audit state at the end of the run: six questions, all explained, with the four recovery-value defects asserted on executed receipts (fabricated self ballot and skipped lower-ballot replies; the empty-slice replacement decided by the reply adopted at the slow-quorum trigger position, final because only N - SlowQuorumSize replies can follow; the status-guard stall cleared only by the executor's retry), the client completion contract holding for the single-NOOP case but not for the empty batch, and the wrong-row write in handlePreAccept refuted as unreachable in this snapshot. Statements, conditions, dependency pointers and citation sets are mutually consistent across the two facts and the behaviour entries, the captured source tree was never modified, and every measurement cited comes from a controller receipt with its fixed experiment, harness and comparison outcomes recorded.
